title: Telegram message
description: Start a run when a Telegram bot receives an update (long polling, not a webhook).
setup: The host polls getUpdates on a schedule and persists the `offset` cursor between calls, passing the last `cursor` back in — Telegram queues nothing once an offset has acknowledged it, so a lost cursor is lost updates. getUpdates and setWebhook are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE for one bot: a host running both gets neither.

request.$comment: A poll trigger CALLS the provider, which is what makes it different in kind from a webhook trigger whose executor only republishes what the host already verified. So this carries a request, exactly like an action does, and the host's obligation is a schedule and a cursor rather than a route and a signature.

resultCheck.$comment: Telegram answers HTTP 200 with {"ok": false, "description": "..."} for application-level failures. A status check alone therefore reads a rejection as a success and publishes an empty batch — a poll that silently finds nothing forever. The connector core cannot know this; it is exactly the per-provider knowledge a definition exists to hold.

poll.$comment: `offset` means "the first update I have NOT handled", so the next cursor is the highest update_id seen plus one. Off by one in either direction is a real bug with no error attached: too low replays updates forever, too high drops one silently.

config.label: Offset
config.description: The first update id NOT yet handled. The HOST persists this between polls and passes the last `cursor` back in — Telegram queues nothing once an offset has acknowledged it.

config.label: Limit
config.description: Updates per poll. Telegram's maximum is 100.

config.label: Update types
config.description: Comma separated. Blank means every type except the chat_member ones, which Telegram requires you to ask for explicitly.

send.$comment: Telegram wants this one as a JSON-encoded array inside a query parameter, not as repeated params — so `list` needs to say how it lands on the wire.

config.label: Sample message (fake mode)
config.description: What the faked update says, so the downstream nodes can be wired before any bot exists.
